summary: Intermittent partial 5xx responses and zero-byte payloads during mixed streaming + embedding burst for enterprise tenant
description:
Issue summary:
Customer NimbusChat reported intermittent spikes of 5xx responses and several zero-byte/empty HTTP responses observed on streaming routes during a large mixed workload with long-running chat streams and concurrent bulk embedding uploads. Errors began at ~11:42 PDT with a steady elevated error rate for ~18 minutes and recurred in short pulses afterwards.

Impact:
- Multiple customer requests from a single enterprise tenant failed with 502/503 and occasional 500s; some streaming sessions returned zero-byte frames and closed connections mid-stream.
- Customer reported degraded UX: partial transcripts and failed embedding batches.
- Tenant on Dedicated pool, SLA impacted.

Environment:
- Prod cluster: us-west-2, dedicated capacity pool dcap-nimbus-3
- API gateway version: apigw-2.14.1
- Serving runtime version: runtime-2026.02.09-hotfix

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Tenant started a burst of mixed workload around 11:40: long-lived streaming chat sessions (keepalive) + parallel embedding bulk upload (concurrent multipart).
2) Accept queue at the API gateway increased and observed connection churn.
3) A subset of streaming connections experienced zero-byte first-chunk responses and then were reset.
4) Upstream runtimes reported transient OOM warnings and watchdog restarts correlated with the window.

Logs and metrics observed:
- apigw.accept_queue_depth spiked to 320 (normal < 40) in us-west-2 region at 11:42.
- apigw.threadpool_queue_time increased to 2.6s.
- apigw returned 502/503 for ~11% of requests from this tenant during the spike.
- runtime.gpu_memory_fragmentation and runtime.prefetch_lock_waits increased concurrently.
- Some runtime pods emitted repeated kalloc OOM logs and then segfaults (nvml resets).
- kvcache.lock_waits rose, several cache-add operations timed out and returned 5xx.

Investigation notes so far:
- Hypothesis A: Mixed long-lived streaming connections plus heavy embedding multipart uploads saturated accept-queue and exhausted proxy thread workers, leading to hedged retries and amplified load on serving runtimes.
- Hypothesis B: A subset of runtime workers experienced GPU memory fragmentation causing out-of-memory conditions when handling embedding fanouts, producing sudden upstream 5xx and short-lived restarts.
- Observed correlation between apigw.accept_queue_depth and runtime OOM events (11:42–11:55).
- Autoscaler did not scale up immediately because dedicated pool was pinned; there was no spare capacity to absorb sudden fanout.
- No recent config rollouts in us-west-2; load pattern appears customer-induced.

Temporary mitigations applied:
- Support applied a temporary tenant rate-limit on large multipart embedding uploads for NimbusChat at 12:03 PDT to reduce arrival rate.
- On-call SRE increased per-tenant connection cap on the proxy for the dedicated pool to reduce accept-queue pressure (short-term).
- Rolled a restart of two affected runtime pods to clear fragmented GPU memory at 12:08; observed partial recovery of error rate.

Next steps / resolution plan:
1) Engineering to add a circuit-breaker in apigw to shed heavy multipart embedding uploads earlier and avoid headroom exhaustion. (Owner: apigw team)
2) Runtime team to investigate GPU memory fragmentation patterns and improve prefetch/kv cache backoff behavior to avoid OOMs under mixed workloads. (Owner: serving-runtime)
3) Product to evaluate throttling guidance and recommend client-side backoff for mixed streaming+embed flows.
4) Add a guardrail in Dedicated provisioning to allow transient burst capacity or better preemption signal to autoscaler for pinned pools. (Owner: infra/autoscaler)
5) Follow up: schedule a post-incident review with NimbusChat and ops teams; propose a configuration change for per-tenant max concurrent multipart uploads.

Resolution notes (in-progress):
- Immediate customer-level workaround: reduced embedding parallelism and implemented retry/backoff in their client.
- Post-fix: target runtime improvements and apigw shed behavior; ETA for mitigations 2 weeks pending prioritization.
